entries.name: W3C Trace Context
entries.status_notes: Standard HTTP headers and value formats for propagating distributed tracing context.
entries.relevance: Provides the most widely applicable starting point for linking one AI task across HTTP service boundaries.
entries.limitations: Propagation can stop or be regenerated at provider boundaries; it does not supply disclosure policy or proof of causality.

entries.name: W3C Trace Context Level 2
entries.status_notes: Adds trace/span ID generation considerations and a random trace-ID flag.
entries.relevance: Random-ID signalling and more explicit ID-generation rules may affect safe cross-domain correlation and sampling.
entries.limitations: Work in progress and not a final W3C Recommendation.

entries.name: W3C Baggage
entries.status_notes: Standard representation and propagation of application-defined properties associated with a distributed workflow.
entries.relevance: Could carry scoped correlation or policy hints that are not part of trace identity.
entries.limitations: High risk of sensitive-data leakage; requires strict allow-listing, size limits, and trust-boundary handling.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions
entries.status_notes: Common meanings and names for telemetry attributes, spans, metrics, events, logs, and resources.
entries.relevance: A shared vocabulary is necessary to combine evidence produced by different implementations.
entries.limitations: Semantic compatibility does not guarantee context propagation, authorisation, retention, or topology mapping.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
entries.status_notes: Still unreleased. On 2026-09-22 main removed the gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram and gen_ai.token.type attribute, replacing them with aggregate gen_ai.client.inference.usage.* counters and per-operation input/output token histograms. Earlier main changes added tool-span conversation IDs and sampling-relevant agent names, renamed cache-creation usage to cache-write usage, removed cache usage from internal invoke_agent spans, and deprecated per-message finish_reason.
evidence: cache-read, cache-write, and reasoning token subsets
entries.relevance: Improves tool-to-conversation correlation and early sampling decisions, and separates aggregate token spend/rate evidence from per-operation distributions, while changing how collectors must interpret token, cache, and completion evidence.
entries.limitations: Experimental main, not a versioned release or stable cross-provider contract. The 2026-09-22 metric replacement is incompatible with collectors expecting gen_ai.client.token.usage. Usage counters report billable tokens when both used and billable values exist; cache, cache-write, and reasoning counters are subsets rather than additional totals. Per-operation histograms omit modality and are for percentiles/outliers, not totals or cost. Conversation identifiers and token usage require disclosure and retention controls, and sampling attributes do not coordinate incident retention across domains.

primary_sources.title: Aggregate and per-operation inference token metrics, 2026-09-22
Remove cache usage from internal invoke_agent spans, 2026-08-27

entries.name: Model Context Protocol trace context propagation
entries.status_notes: The MCP project released the 2026-07-28 specification on 2026-07-28, and its versioning page identifies that version as current and ready for use. This corrects the catalogue's release-candidate label, not a September release. SEP-414 remains Final and documents W3C trace context and baggage in JSON-RPC `_meta`; official SDK documentation describes propagation and spans.
entries.relevance: Provides a protocol-defined carrier for following agent-to-tool requests across MCP clients, servers, and gateways, directly reducing a documented task-correlation gap.
entries.limitations: Published MCP project specification, not an IETF or W3C standard. SEP-414 defines conventions without requiring every implementation to propagate or emit them; SDK coverage and API stability vary. Correlation metadata still needs trust-boundary and data-minimisation policy.

primary_sources.title: MCP SEP-414 trace context propagation conventions
MCP specification versioning and current version

entries.name: OpenMetrics 1.0
entries.status_notes: Stable metric exposition format with broad Prometheus ecosystem adoption.
entries.relevance: A common metric format can carry inference, compute, and network health evidence between collection systems.
entries.limitations: Aggregated time series often cannot explain the critical path of one transaction.

entries.name: OpenMetrics 2.0
entries.status_notes: Second-generation OpenMetrics work with improved alignment to the OpenTelemetry data model and naming conventions.
entries.relevance: Potentially improves interoperability between inference metrics, Prometheus systems, and OpenTelemetry.
entries.limitations: Experimental at baseline; compatibility and production adoption are not established.

entries.name: vLLM metrics, tracing, and per-request metrics
entries.version: v0.30.0 stable; Responses per-request metrics remain main-only
entries.status_notes: v0.30.0 was released 2026-09-22. It ships the clarified streamed-event inter-token latency versus per-request time-per-output-token semantics and a HiSparse host-resident KV-cache tier with Prometheus counters for device hot-buffer hits, misses, and host-to-device bytes. Per-request timing for /v1/responses, merged 2026-09-16, is absent from the v0.30.0 tag and remains main-only. Existing OpenTelemetry tracing and experimental opt-in speculative-decoding acceptance metrics remain.
evidence: HiSparse hot-buffer cache hits and misses
Responses API per-request timing on main
entries.relevance: Separates inference-side queue, execution, streaming, speculative-decoding, and one implementation's host-resident KV-cache behaviour that otherwise appear as one network-visible request time.
entries.limitations: Responses support remains main-only: metrics arrive on the non-streaming response or final response.completed event and are suppressed for multi-generation tool turns. Per-request timing requires --enable-per-request-metrics and enabled statistics, with possible CPU overhead. HiSparse counters are implementation-specific, collected asynchronously through the KV-connector statistics path every 2,000 steps, and do not establish transferable cache state or cross-provider semantics. Speculative acceptance fields remain experimental, opt-in, and single-sequence. Output events may contain multiple tokens, so inter-token latency and per-request TPOT have different weighting. Timing and cache evidence can expose workload characteristics and require access and disclosure controls.

primary_sources.title: vLLM per-request speculative decoding acceptance metrics
Responses API per-request metrics merged on main, 2026-09-16
HiSparse Prometheus counters merged for v0.30.0

entries.name: NVIDIA Triton metrics and tracing
entries.status_notes: Provides Prometheus request/GPU/cache metrics and per-request tracing using Triton or OpenTelemetry modes.
entries.relevance: Provides inference and accelerator evidence that can be correlated with task and network observations.
entries.limitations: Telemetry configuration, naming, sampling, retention, and visibility are deployment-specific.

entries.name: OpenConfig gNMI
entries.version: 0.11.0 in revision history; document header states 0.10.0
entries.status_notes: The March 2026 revision history adds v0.11.0, while the visible specification header still reports v0.10.0 and 0.10.x compatibility.
entries.relevance: Supplies detailed device and interface evidence needed to separate path/device degradation from compute delay.
entries.limitations: Local device paths and counters need topology and transaction mapping; the baseline source has an internal version inconsistency.

entries.name: YANG-Push
entries.status_notes: Subscription and push mechanisms for YANG datastore updates, including on-change notifications.
entries.relevance: Can publish modelled network and on-path telemetry without continuous polling.
entries.limitations: Data models, access control, topology mapping, and cross-domain correlation remain separate concerns.

primary_sources.title: RFC 8641: Subscription to YANG Notifications for Datastore Updates

entries.name: IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX)
entries.status_notes: Standards-track protocol for exporting traffic-flow information from exporters to collectors.
entries.relevance: Shows who communicated, when, and at what scale across network boundaries.
entries.limitations: Sampling and aggregation can obscure short incidents; flow identity does not establish application causality.

entries.name: BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP)
entries.status_notes: Provides route views and BGP session monitoring; active work includes BMP v4/TLV and routing-event extensions.
entries.relevance: Can place routing changes on the same timeline as application and inference degradation.
entries.limitations: Temporal coincidence is not causal proof; visibility depends on where BMP is collected.

entries.name: STAMP and TWAMP
entries.status_notes: Active measurement protocols for one-way and round-trip performance metrics.
entries.relevance: Provides controlled path-performance evidence independent of application and inference instrumentation.
entries.limitations: Probe paths and treatment may differ from the transaction; one-way interpretation depends on time quality.

primary_sources.title: RFC 8762: Simple Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol

entries.name: In Situ OAM (IOAM)
entries.status_notes: Defines on-path operational and telemetry data fields for use inside limited IOAM domains, with direct-export and encapsulation extensions.
entries.relevance: Can produce fine-grained path evidence that complements active probes and device counters.
entries.limitations: Limited-domain model, deployment overhead, integrity, privacy, and cross-domain disclosure constraints.

entries.name: IETF Network Telemetry Framework
entries.status_notes: Taxonomy and framework covering telemetry acquisition, export, analysis, and techniques including active, passive, and hybrid measurement.
entries.relevance: Provides a standards-based map for the network portion of the observability landscape.
entries.limitations: Does not define a cross-domain task-correlation or disclosure protocol.

entries.name: On-Path Telemetry YANG Data Model
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group draft revised 2026-08-26. Revision -06 redesigns the module to augment the existing AltMark and IOAM YANG models rather than duplicate their configuration structure.
evidence: Alternate Marking loss and delay data
IOAM trace, proof-of-transit, direct-export, and edge-to-edge data
entries.relevance: Makes selected on-path evidence available through model-driven telemetry and YANG-Push while aligning it with existing AltMark and IOAM configuration models.
entries.limitations: Work in progress and limited to Alternate Marking and IOAM. The revision does not define cross-domain identifier scope, clock-quality metadata, task correlation, or disclosure policy; an early performance-metrics review still records the draft as not ready.

entries.name: Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS) Framework
entries.status_notes: IETF framework for combining network and computing-resource information when selecting a service instance; baseline framework covers one service provider.
entries.relevance: Directly overlaps the talk's hypothesis that live network and compute signals may influence inference placement.
entries.limitations: Framework scope and single-provider assumption do not solve multi-provider observability or federation.

primary_sources.title: A Framework for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering

entries.name: CATS YANG Data Model
entries.status_notes: CATS working-group -00 approved and posted 2026-09-23, replacing draft-yl-cats-data-model. The Standards Track work defines an ietf-cats YANG module that augments ietf-routing with CATS base policy, traffic classifiers, service-instance metrics, operational counters, and limit notifications.
evidence: service-instance source, priority, affinity, and location
extensible service metric type and value
matched and forwarded packet and byte counters
entries.relevance: Provides a concrete model-driven mapping between CATS services, service instances, topology locations, steering inputs, and operational counters, directly narrowing the documented topology and service-mapping gap.
entries.limitations: Working-group draft, not an RFC, with no implementation or interoperability evidence found. It operates within the CATS framework's provider scope and does not map an AI task to a service instance across domains. Metric meanings depend on separate extensible definitions, and the model does not supply shared time quality, evidence integrity, or disclosure policy. Writable state can affect routing and readable state can reveal sensitive service and topology information.

primary_sources.title: Data Model for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS), revision -00
CATS data-model document history and working-group approval, 2026-09-23

entries.name: CATS OAM Framework
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group draft dated 2026-07-21 covering fault management and performance monitoring across clients, network paths, and service instances.
entries.relevance: One of the closest current standards efforts to joint network-and-compute causal evidence.
entries.limitations: Early work in progress; data models, cross-domain trust, and implementation experience remain open.

entries.name: CATS OAM Use Cases and Requirements
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-07-31; it has no formal IETF standing at baseline.
entries.relevance: Provides operator-oriented scenarios against which FOX and other cross-domain models can be tested.
entries.limitations: Individual draft, not IETF consensus; must be treated as a discovery source and working proposal.

primary_sources.title: CATS OAM Use Cases and Requirements

entries.name: Quality of Outcome (QoO)
entries.status_notes: IETF working-group document in advanced processing at baseline; defines application-specific network quality assessment and outcome scores.
entries.relevance: May help translate network measurements into an application-facing signal suitable for placement or troubleshooting.
entries.limitations: A quality score does not identify the causal component and may hide distribution or measurement assumptions.

entries.name: Transport Considerations for Large-Scale Distributed Inference Networks
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-07-04; it has no formal IETF standing at baseline.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses traffic generated by disaggregated and expert-parallel inference and may produce new measurement requirements.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal focused largely on large-scale inference networks; it must not be presented as consensus or general WAN evidence.

primary_sources.title: Transport Considerations for Large-Scale Distributed Inference Networks

entries.name: Proxy Modes for Agent-Tool Protocols
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft published 2026-08-13 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes W3C trace propagation, append-only hop metadata, and intermediary metrics for agent-tool protocol proxies.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses observability across agent-tool intermediaries and makes routing, retry, partial-failure, and gateway-hop behaviour more visible.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no IETF consensus or demonstrated interoperable implementation; its hop metadata may expose topology and requires integrity, privacy, and bounded-disclosure controls.

entries.name: Temporal Integrity Metadata (TIM) for Infrastructure Telemetry
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft dated 2026-08-08 and last updated 2026-08-10; it has no formal IETF standing. It proposes transport-agnostic metadata describing the temporal integrity of telemetry observations.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses the documented need to qualify timestamps from heterogeneous application, inference, and network evidence before constructing a causal timeline.
entries.limitations: Work in progress with no working-group adoption, consensus, transport binding, interoperability evidence, or known implementation. Quality is self-declared; the draft does not synchronise clocks, guarantee declared accuracy, or establish causal order, and integrity and disclosure policy remain deployment concerns.

primary_sources.title: Temporal Integrity Metadata (TIM) for Infrastructure Telemetry

entries.name: Scoping and Comparability Requirements for Exported Network Telemetry Identifiers
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revised 2026-09-04; it has no formal IETF standing. Revision -01 substantially replaces the earlier vocabulary-centric structure with broader requirements for defining the scope and comparability of telemetry identifiers and statistics.
entries.relevance: Directly addresses semantic ambiguity that can cause collectors to merge unrelated records, compare incommensurate values, or construct invalid cross-domain evidence timelines.
entries.limitations: Work in progress with no working-group adoption, consensus, wire format, data model, implementation, or interoperability evidence. Revision -01 no longer defines the four named scope values or omitted-identifier default from -00; its abstract says scope and comparison conditions MUST be explicit while the requirements section says identifiers or statistics SHOULD define them, so normative strength remains uncertain. Declared scope also does not authenticate or independently verify identity, time, or integrity.

primary_sources.title: Scoping and Comparability Requirements for Exported Network Telemetry Identifiers

entries.name: Data Manifest for Contextualized Telemetry Data
entries.status_notes: IETF OPSAWG document revision -15 completed IETF Last Call on 2026-09-26, when its IESG state changed from In Last Call to Waiting for AD Go-Ahead. It remains under review for publication as a Proposed Standard and specifies metadata for preserving the interpretation context of collected network telemetry.
entries.relevance: Makes YANG telemetry more defensible for later analysis by binding observations to the platform, schema, subscription, and collection conditions under which they were produced.
entries.limitations: Not yet approved or published as an RFC. IANA's 2026-09-25 review requires expert review before approval. The Platform Manifest and current-period augmentation are normative, but the Data Collection Manifest remains a non-normative example because YANG lacks design-time schema mount. Data lineage, task correlation, cross-domain disclosure policy, and proof that metadata is accurate are out of scope.

primary_sources.title: A Data Manifest for Contextualized Telemetry Data
Data Manifest document history and IESG state transition, 2026-09-26

entries.name: Agent Run Metrics
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft published 2026-09-10 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes a JSON interchange report for resource accounting and execution structure of language-model agent runs.
evidence: timing, status, termination, and error metadata
W3C trace ID and span ID bindings
entries.relevance: Directly addresses the documented need for retry and delegation lineage and offers a candidate vocabulary for joining per-run agent activity to distributed traces without including prompts, completions, tool arguments, or tool results.
entries.limitations: Early individual proposal with no IETF consensus, working-group adoption, known implementation, or interoperability evidence. Reports are assertions by the reporter rather than independently verified consumption evidence; signatures, provider reconciliation, and authentication mechanisms are out of scope. Counters and persistent run identifiers can still disclose sensitive activity patterns and require retention, namespace, size, and rate controls.

primary_sources.title: Agent Run Metrics: A JSON Interchange Format for Resource Accounting of Language-Model Agent Runs

entries.name: BMP Statistics Information TLV
entries.status_notes: IETF GROW working-group draft revised 2026-09-11. Revision -01 changes the proposed wire layout with measurement-window duration, sample count, and microsecond-resolution extrema timestamps; it adds percentile entries and constrains interpretation to gauge statistics.
evidence: snapshot, mean, median, and percentile statistics
entries.relevance: Can preserve short routing-state excursions between exports and make statistical comparison assumptions explicit.
entries.limitations: Not an RFC; incompatible draft wire changes and no implementation evidence found. Comparisons require compatible collection settings; the draft does not export collection methodology or mandate a percentile algorithm. Unsigned exporter assertions and sensitive router dynamics require integrity, access, and disclosure controls.

primary_sources.title: BMP Statistics Information TLV, revision -01 dated 2026-09-11

entries.name: STAMP IP and IPv6 Extension Header Reflection
entries.status_notes: IETF IPPM working-group draft revised 2026-09-18. Revision -14 requires received headers to reach the measurement endpoints and makes header selection, no-match reporting, reverse-direction construction, and MTU accounting more explicit.
evidence: reflected IP and IPv6 extension headers
entries.relevance: Connects active probes with selected on-path header evidence while clarifying interoperability requirements.
entries.limitations: Not an RFC or proof of transaction causality. The draft cites Teaparty implementation, but its linked 2025-06-09 commit targets revision -04; -14 conformance is not established. Limited-domain use, header disclosure, reflection amplification, data-plane access, and MTU constraints remain deployment concerns.

primary_sources.title: STAMP IP and IPv6 Extension Header Reflection, revision -14 dated 2026-09-18

entries.name: Agent Operation Continuity Across Executor Replacement
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft published 2026-09-15 with no formal IETF standing. It proposes continuity requirements for operation identity, immutable provider bindings, attempt evidence, unresolved outcomes, and stale-executor fencing.
entries.relevance: Addresses evidence loss and unsafe reinterpretation when an agent executor fails or is replaced.
entries.limitations: One authoritative coordination domain only; no universal identifier, evidence format, or cross-domain ledger migration. The draft reports same-team local and synthetic-provider testing, not live-provider deployment or independent interoperability. Provider assertions do not prove outcomes; persistent identifiers and request digests need minimisation, access, and retention controls.

primary_sources.title: Agent Operation Continuity Across Executor Replacement, 2026-09-15

entries.name: AI Audit Reference Architecture for Post-Hoc Agent Accountability
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft revision -01 dated 2026-09-21; it has no formal IETF standing. The revision adds confirmation windows, live parent-credential revalidation, explicit producer-unavailability policy, independently observed effects, audience binding, a separately redactable content container, and a sixth verification check, while expanding security and completeness gaps.
evidence: signed log commitments and external registration
verified, accepted, bound, existence, coverage, and ordering checks
producer failure and out-of-band anomaly handling
entries.relevance: Addresses the trust, integrity, and recipient-disclosure gaps in post-hoc cross-organisational evidence.
entries.limitations: Reference architecture, not a deployed exchange protocol or real-time authorisation mechanism. The author reports informal sample-code testing, but no published implementation, formal model, or interoperability evidence was found. Revision -01 explicitly leaves declared-scope evasion, tail truncation and same-length forks, confirmation-window sizing, human-authority bootstrapping, observer compromise, denial of service, and formal verification unresolved. Signatures still cannot establish completeness or outcome truth.

primary_sources.title: AI Audit Reference Architecture for Post-Hoc Agent Accountability, revision -01 dated 2026-09-21

entries.name: Audit Record Format for AI Agent Authorization Decisions
entries.status_notes: Individual Internet-Draft first posted as -00 on 2026-09-21 and revised to -01 on 2026-09-27; it has no formal IETF standing. It defines an in-toto predicate in a DSSE envelope with RFC 8785 canonicalization, fields mapped to the WIMSE AIMS audit requirements, and verifier-derived decision/effect agreement.
evidence: agent, delegation, resource, and request binding
agree, disagree, not-exercised, and indeterminate outcomes
conformance vectors specified in the draft
entries.relevance: Supplies a concrete candidate record and verification algorithm for correlating authorization decisions with independently observed effects across a service boundary, narrowing the common-vocabulary and trust/integrity gaps.
entries.limitations: Individual proposal with no working-group adoption, IETF consensus, published implementation, or interoperability result; the Datatracker records a related IPR disclosure. Its predicate URI is author-controlled and unregistered with IANA. The companion registry says the Appendix B vectors are not yet published. A claimed observation vantage is not self-proving, a producer can withhold whole records, and a valid signature or internally coherent record does not prove completeness or external truth. Identifiers, paths, and timing can disclose sensitive activity and require policy and minimisation.

primary_sources.title: An Audit Record Format for AI Agent Authorization Decisions, revision -01
Document history showing -00 and -01 publication dates
Author-controlled predicate registry and conformance-corpus status

entries.name: Federated Observability Exchange (FOX)
entries.status_notes: Project hypothesis for neutral, policy-controlled exchange of selected cross-domain evidence.
entries.relevance: Explores whether neutral interconnection can address the coordination gap left by domain-local observability tools.
entries.limitations: No protocol, implementation, deployment, or independent validation exists at baseline.
